for multiple building material dealers.</span></ix:nonNumeric></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000301" name="hbp:CollectiveBargainingAgreementsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true">Collective Bargaining Agreements<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">&#8212;As of December 31, 2020, approximately <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000345" name="hbp:CollectiveBargainingArrangementPercentageOfParticipants" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2">12</ix:nonFraction>% of our employees were represented by <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_hbpAgreement" id="F_000347" name="hbp:NumberOfCollectiveBargainingAgreementExpiredInNextYear" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_hbpAgreement" id="F_000346" name="hbp:NumberOfCollectiveBargainingAgreements" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">seven</ix:nonFraction> collective bargaining agreements.</span><span style="Background-color:#B2A1C7;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> </span></ix:nonNumeric></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000302" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true">Segments<span style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;">&#8212;Operating segments are components of an enterprise for which separate financial information is available and evaluated regularly by the chief operating decision maker in deciding how to allocate resources and in assessing performance.  At December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, under the definition of a segment, each of our distribution centers is considered an operating segment of our business.  Operating segments may be aggregated if the operating segments have similar economic characteristics and if the nature of the products, distribution methods, customers and regulatory environments are similar.  The Company has aggregated its distribution centers into <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_hbpSegment" id="F_000348" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_hbpSegment" id="F_000349" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" contextRef="C_0001093082_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> reporting segment.</span></ix:nonNumeric></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000268" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsAndChangesInAccountingPrinciplesTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;NEW ACCOUNTING STANDARDS</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Adoption of New Accounting Standards</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000351" name="us-gaap:ChangeInAccountingPrincipleAccountingStandardsUpdateAdoptionDate" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201613Member_20201231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">January 1, 2020</ix:nonNumeric>, the Company adopted ASU 2016-13, &#8220;Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments.&#8221; ASU 2016-13 requires a financial asset (or a group of financial assets) measured at amortized cost basis to be assessed for impairment under the current expected credit loss model rather than an incurred loss model. The measurement of expected credit losses is based on relevant information about past events, including historical experience, current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts that affect the collectability of the reported amount.&#160; The primary financial asset of the Company within the scope of ASU 2016-13 is trade receivables.&#160; The adoption of ASU 2016-13 did not materially impact the Company's consolidated financial statements.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000354" name="us-gaap:ChangeInAccountingPrincipleAccountingStandardsUpdateAdoptionDate" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201602Member_20201231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">January 1, 2019</ix:nonNumeric>, the Company adopted ASU 2016-02, &#8220;Leases (Topic 842),&#8221; which requires lessees to recognize leases on-balance sheet and disclose key information about leasing arrangements.&#160;&#160;The new standard establishes a right-of-use (&#8220;ROU&#8221;) model that requires a lessee to recognize a ROU asset and a lease liability on the balance sheet for all leases with a term longer than 12 months.&#160;&#160;Leases will be classified as financing or operating, with classification affecting the pattern and classification of expense recognition in the income statement.&#160;&#160;The Company adopted the standard on its effective date using the modified retrospective approach and a package of practical expedients permitted by the transition guidance of the new standard.&#160;&#160;The practical expedients included an accounting policy election to forgo recognition of ROU asset and liability on leases with an initial term of 12 months or less, and to forgo separate recognition of lease and non-lease components for all leases.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000357" name="us-gaap:ChangeInAccountingPrincipleAccountingStandardsUpdateAdoptionDate" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201807Member_20201231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">January 1, 2019</ix:nonNumeric>, the Company adopted ASU 2018-07, &#8220;Improvements to Nonemployee Share-Based Payment Accounting.&#8221;&#160;&#160;ASU 2018-07 more closely aligns the accounting for employee and nonemployee share-based payments.&#160;&#160;There was no material impact to stock-based compensation, income from continuing operations after taxes, net income or earnings per share as a result of adoption.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company adopted the amendments to certain disclosure requirements in Securities Act of 1933, as amended, Release No. 33-10532, &#8220;Disclosure Update and Simplification&#8221; on November 5, 2018, the effective date of the release. Among the amendments is a requirement to present the changes in shareholders&#8217; equity in the interim financial statements (either in a separate statement or footnote) in quarterly reports on Form 10-Q. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accounting Standards Issued But Not Yet Adopted</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent accounting pronouncements pending adoption and not discussed above are either not applicable or will not have, or are not expected to have, a material impact on our consolidated financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows. </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000269" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000269_dcnt_d8dec55d-2b6a-4671-9531-f0d640fcc4a1">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;REVENUE</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Revenue is measured as the amount of consideration the Company expects to receive in exchange for transferring goods.&#160;&#160;The Company reports sales revenue, including direct sales, on a net basis, which includes gross </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">-37-</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000269_dcnt_d8dec55d-2b6a-4671-9531-f0d640fcc4a1">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">revenue adjustments for estimated returns, cash payment discounts based on the satisfaction of outstanding receivables, and volume purchase rebates.&#160;&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s</span><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> customer payment terms are typical for our industry&#59; these terms vary by customer and location, as well as by the products purchased.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Regarding direct sales, the Company is the principal in the arrangement and is responsible for fulfilling the promise to provide specific goods to its customers, including product specifications, pricing and modifications prior to delivery.&#160;&#160;Direct sales, as a percentage of net sales, were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000361" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_us-gaapSalesRevenueNetMember_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_us-gaapCustomerConcentrationRiskMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2">18</ix:nonFraction>%, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000359" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_us-gaapSalesRevenueNetMember_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_us-gaapCustomerConcentrationRiskMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="2" scale="-2">18</ix:nonFraction>%, and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000360" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis_us-gaapSalesRevenueNetMember_us-gaapConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis_us-gaapCustomerConcentrationRiskMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="2" scale="-2">19</ix:nonFraction>% in each of the years ended December 31, 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively. </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000303" name="us-gaap:DisaggregationOfRevenueTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">4.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;LEASES</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:7.69%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has operating and financing leases for corporate offices, distribution centers, vehicles, and certain equipment. These leases have remaining lease terms of less than <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000374" name="hbp:LesseeOperatingAndFinancingLeasesRemainingLeaseTerm" contextRef="C_0001093082_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1</ix:nonNumeric> year to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000375" name="hbp:LesseeOperatingAndFinancingLeasesRemainingLeaseTerm" contextRef="C_0001093082_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">12</ix:nonNumeric> years and many of the leases have renewal options.&#160;&#160;Because the Company is not reasonably certain to exercise the renewal options, generally the options are not considered in determining the lease term, and associated potential option payments are excluded from lease payments and right-of-use calculations.&#160;&#160;Leases with an initial term of 12 months or less are excluded from right-of-use calculations, and we do not separately recognize the lease and non-lease components of lease agreements.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:7.69%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition to fixed payments, many of the Company&#8217;s lease contracts contain variable payments. Vehicle lease variable payments typically include mileage, and real estate leases include variable charges for taxes and common area maintenance.&#160;&#160;Variable lease payments and payments for leases with an initial term of 12 months or less are recognized in the period incurred.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000304" name="us-gaap:LeaseCostTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:7.69%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2020, the weighted average remaining lease term for the Company&#8217;s operating leases was <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000408" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageRemainingLeaseTerm1" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">5.0</ix:nonNumeric> years and for its financing leases was <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000409" name="us-gaap:FinanceLeaseWeightedAverageRemainingLeaseTerm1" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">2.9</ix:nonNumeric> years. These leases have weighted average discount rates of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000410" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageDiscountRatePercent" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">5.21</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000411" name="us-gaap:FinanceLeaseWeightedAverageDiscountRatePercent" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">6.19</ix:nonFraction>% for operating leases and financing leases, respectively. The rate implicit in the lease is used to discount leases when known. While the implicit rate is often known for finance leases, the Company is generally unable to calculate the implicit rate in operating leases because it does not have access to the lessor&#8217;s residual value estimates nor the amount of the lessor&#8217;s deferred initial direct costs.&#160;&#160;When the implicit rate is not known, the Company uses the incremental borrowing rate for secured loans of similar term. The Company uses available data for unsecured loans to borrowers of similar credit to the Company and adjusts the rate to reflect the effect of providing collateral equivalent to the outstanding obligation balance.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000306" name="hbp:ScheduleOfSupplementalCashFlowInformationRelatedToLeasesTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">5.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;GOODWILL AND OTHER INTANGIBLE ASSETS</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill is reviewed for impairment annually, or more frequently if certain indicators arise. The Company assesses each reporting period whether events and circumstances warrant a revision to the previously established useful lives.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the first quarter of 2020, a decline in the market value of the Company&#8217;s public equity concurrent with and partially resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic triggered an assessment of goodwill. The fair value of each reporting unit was determined using a market approach to consider factors such as market capitalization of the Company at March 31, 2020, observed ratios of enterprise value to earnings, and the relative sales contribution of each reporting unit. If a reporting unit&#8217;s carrying value exceeded its estimated fair value, an impairment was recorded for the amount in excess. As a result of the interim goodwill impairment test, the Company recognized a goodwill impairment charge of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000435" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">9.5</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160;&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5.24%;text-indent:-5.24%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5.24%;text-indent:-5.24%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000276" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000276_dcnt_62788871-52e7-4558-a627-fcfd07052478">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Legal and Environmental Matters</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company accrues expenses for contingencies when it is probable that an asset has been impaired or a liability has been incurred and management can reasonably estimate the expense.  Contingencies for which the Company has made accruals include environmental and other legal matters.  It is possible, however, that actual expenses could exceed our accrual by a material amount which could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s future liquidity, financial condition or operating results in the period in which any such additional expenses are incurred or recognized.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Environmental Matters</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company was previously identified as a potentially responsible party in connection with the cleanup of contamination at a formerly owned property in Montana.  On February&#160;18, 2015, the Montana Department of Environmental Quality (the &#8220;DEQ&#8221;) issued an amendment to the unilateral administrative order of the DEQ outlining </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">-42-</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000276_dcnt_62788871-52e7-4558-a627-fcfd07052478">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the final remediation of the property in its Record of Decision (the &#8220;ROD&#8221;).&#160;&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In September 2015, the remedial action work plan (&#8220;RAWP&#8221;) was approved. </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.81%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company paid $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000559" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingenciesPayments1" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.2</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000560" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingenciesPayments1" contextRef="C_0001093082_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000561" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingenciesPayments1" contextRef="C_0001093082_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.6</ix:nonFraction> million in 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively, for costs related to implementation of the RAWP.&#160;&#160;While the Company expects ongoing remediation expenditures to continue, it is unable to ascertain the timeline for completion given the uncertain nature of projects of this type.&#160;&#160;Following subsequent reviews of the remaining costs to complete the remediation, the Company recorded a charge of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000558" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingenciesChargesToExpenseForNewLosses" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapDisposalGroupClassificationAxis_us-gaapSegmentDiscontinuedOperationsMember_20181001_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in the fourth quarter of 2018 which was reflected in discontinued operations.  The Company estimates the total remaining cost of implementing the RAWP to be $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000557" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingencies" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapBalanceSheetLocationAxis_hbpOtherAccruedLiabilitiesAndOtherNoncurrentLiabilitiesMember_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at December&#160;31, 2020 and this amount is accrued in &#8220;other accrued liabilities&#8221; and &#8220;other non-current liabilities&#8221; on the consolidated balance sheets.  The Company believes the accrual represents a reasonable best estimate of the total remaining remediation costs, based on facts, circumstances, and information currently available.&#160;&#160;However, there are currently unknown variables relating to the actual levels of contaminants and amounts of soil that will ultimately require treatment or removal and as part of the remediation process, additional soil and groundwater sampling, and bench and pilot testing is required to ensure the remediation will achieve the outcome required by the DEQ.&#160;&#160;The ultimate final amount of remediation costs and expenditures are difficult to estimate with certainty and as a result, the amount of actual costs and expenses ultimately incurred by the Company with respect to this property could be lower than, or exceed the amount accrued as of December&#160;31, 2020 by a material amount.&#160;&#160;If actual costs are materially higher, the incremental expenses over the amount currently accrued could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial condition and operating results.&#160;&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">With the consent of the DEQ, remediation efforts and expenditures were temporarily suspended during the pandemic in 2020 based on health, safety, financial and other considerations.&#160;&#160;The Company has agreed with the DEQ to resume remediation activities in 2021.&#160;&#160;See Note 18, &#8220;Impact of and Company Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic.&#8221;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition, some of the Company&#8217;s current and former distribution centers are located in areas where environmental contamination may have occurred, and for which the Company, among others, could be held responsible.  The Company currently believes that there are no material environmental liabilities at any of its distribution center locations.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.62%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Legal Matters</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is party to various litigation matters, in most cases involving ordinary and routine claims incidental to its business. It cannot reasonably estimate the ultimate legal and financial liability with respect to all pending litigation matters. However, the Company believes, based on our examination of such matters, that the ultimate liability will not have a material adverse effect on its financial position, results of operation or cash flows. </p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the 2005 Executive Incentive Compensation Plan, as amended and restated (the &#8220;2005 Plan&#8221;), the Company may grant up to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000591" name="hbp:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfCommonStockExpectedToBeGrant" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hbpTwoThousandFiveExecutiveIncentiveCompensationPlanMember_20171231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">8,125,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock to be used as incentive awards.&#160;&#160;The 2005 Plan allows the Company to grant awards to key employees, including restricted stock awards, stock options, other stock-based incentive awards and cash-based incentive awards subject primarily to the requirement of continued employment. Awards under the 2005 Plan are available for grant over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000592">ten-year</span> period unless terminated earlier by the Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;The Company granted <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000593" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hbpTwoThousandFiveExecutiveIncentiveCompensationPlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">480,325</ix:nonFraction>, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000594" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hbpTwoThousandFiveExecutiveIncentiveCompensationPlanMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">510,684</ix:nonFraction>, and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000595" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hbpTwoThousandFiveExecutiveIncentiveCompensationPlanMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">406,743</ix:nonFraction> shares of restricted stock to employees in 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively.&#160;&#160;No monetary consideration is paid to the Company by employees who receive restricted stock. The restricted shares vest ratably over three to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000597" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001093082_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_hbpTwoThousandFiveExecutiveIncentiveCompensationPlanMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric>.&#160;&#160;Restricted stock can be granted with or without performance restrictions.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December&#160;31, 2020, our valuation allowance on deferred tax assets (&#8220;DTAs&#8221;) was approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000681" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">18.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million compared to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000682" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001093082_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">20.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at December&#160;31, 2019.  In each reporting period, we assess the available positive and negative evidence to estimate if sufficient future taxable income would be generated to utilize the existing deferred tax assets. Starting in 2019, our operations were in a position of cumulative losses for the most recent three-year period. The cumulative loss incurred by the Company over the three-year period ended December 31, 2019 constitutes a significant piece of objective negative evidence.&#160;&#160;Such objective negative evidence limits the ability to consider other subjective evidence, such as our projections for future profitability and growth.&#160;&#160;Based on this evaluation, the company concluded primarily that it is more likely than not that a significant portion of our deferred tax assets will not be realized. Accordingly, the Company recorded a full valuation allowance on its net deferred tax asset position, resulting in a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000683" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" contextRef="C_0001093082_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">12.7</ix:nonFraction> million income tax expense in our provision for income taxes in 2019. The Company maintained the cumulative loss for the most recent three-year period as of December 31, 2020. Before we change our judgement on the need for a valuation allowance, a sustained period of operating profitability is required.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The income tax expense from continuing operations for 2020 was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000684" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million on a loss before taxes of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000686" name="us-gaap:IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesExtraordinaryItemsNoncontrollingInterest" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">0.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.  For 2019, an income tax expense of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000685" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="C_0001093082_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">11.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million was recorded on a pretax loss of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000687" name="us-gaap:IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsBeforeIncomeTaxesExtraordinaryItemsNoncontrollingInterest" contextRef="C_0001093082_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">10.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2020, the Company had gross deferred tax assets of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000688" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsGross" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">32.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and a valuation allowance of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000689" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">18.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, netting to deferred tax assets of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000690" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsNet" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">14.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.  The Company had deferred tax liabilities of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000691" name="us-gaap:DeferredIncomeTaxLiabilities" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">14.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at December 31, 2020.  The Company had <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000692" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsLiabilitiesNet" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000693" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsLiabilitiesNet" contextRef="C_0001093082_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> net deferred tax assets at both December 31, 2020 and 2019. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On March 27, 2020, the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act ("the Act") was signed into law, making several changes to the Internal Revenue Code. The changes included, but are not limited to increasing the limitation on the amount of deduction interest expense under Code Section 163(j), allowing companies to carry back certain net operating losses, and increasing the amount of net operating loss carryforwards that corporations can use to offset taxable income. The Company benefited from these changes with an additional interest expense deduction of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000694" name="hbp:IncomeTaxReconciliationAdditionalInterestExpenseDeduction" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">4.3</ix:nonFraction> million in 2020.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000280" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000280_dcnt_ce530e82-1e53-46ef-9edb-8e04ba3e773b">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">14.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;BASIC AND DILUTED NET LOSS PER SHARE</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company calculates its basic loss per share by dividing net loss allocated to common shares outstanding by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding.&#160;&#160;Unvested shares of restricted stock participate in dividends on the same basis as common shares.  As a result, these share-based awards meet the definition of participating securities and the Company applies the two-class method to compute earnings per share.  The two-class method is an earnings allocation formula that treats participating securities as having rights to earnings that would otherwise have been available to common stockholders.  In periods in which the Company has net losses, the losses are not allocated to participating securities because the participating security holders are not obligated to share in such losses.&#160;&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000320" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfEarningsPerShareBasicByCommonClassTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000320_cnt_1">The following table presents the number of participating securities and earnings allocated to those securities for the years ended December 31, 2020, 2019 and 2018 (in millions):</ix:nonNumeric></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000281" name="hbp:RightsAgreementTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">15.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;RIGHTS AGREEMENT</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On May 18, 2016, the Board of Directors (the &#8220;Board&#8221;) of the Company entered into a rights agreement (the &#8220;Rights Agreement&#8221;) with Computershare Trust Company, N.A. and declared a dividend of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000750" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockConversionBasis" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231">one preferred share purchase right (a &#8220;Right&#8221;) for each outstanding share of common stock</ix:nonNumeric>, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_000751" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" contextRef="C_0001093082_20160518" decimals="INF">0.01</ix:nonFraction> par value per share, of the Company.&#160;&#160;The dividend was paid at close of business on <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000752" name="us-gaap:DividendPayableDateToBePaidDayMonthAndYear" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">May&#160;31, 2016</ix:nonNumeric> to the stockholders of record on that date.&#160;&#160;The Board adopted the Rights Agreement to protect stockholder value by protecting the Company&#8217;s ability to capture the value of its net operating losses used to reduce potential future federal income tax obligations.  The Rights Agreement was approved by the Company&#8217;s stockholders at the 2017 annual meeting of stockholders.&#160;&#160;On May 6, 2019 the Board approved and we entered into a First Amendment to Rights Agreement between the Company and ComputerShare Trust Company, N.A., as rights agent. The Amendment, among other things, (i) extends the final expiration date (as defined in the Rights Agreement) from <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000753" name="hbp:RightsAgreementExpirationDate" contextRef="C_0001093082_20190505_20190505" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">May 18, 2019</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000754" name="hbp:RightsAgreementExpirationDate" contextRef="C_0001093082_20190506_20190506" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">May 18, 2022</ix:nonNumeric>&#59; (ii) changes the initial purchase price (as defined in the Rights Agreement) from $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_000755" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" contextRef="C_0001093082_20190505" decimals="2">13.86</ix:nonFraction> to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_000756" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" contextRef="C_0001093082_20190506" decimals="2">13.39</ix:nonFraction>&#59; and (iii) increases the period pursuant to which the Board has to consider an exemption request (as defined in the Rights Agreement) from ten business days to 20 business days.&#160;&#160;The Rights Agreement will expire on the earliest of (i) May 18, 2022, (ii) the time at which the Rights are redeemed or exchanged, as provided for in the Rights Agreement, (iii) the repeal of Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, if the Board determines that the Rights Agreement is no longer necessary for the preservation of the Company&#8217;s NOLs, and (iv) the beginning of a taxable year of the Company to which the Board determines that no NOLs may be carried forward. We<span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;"> adopted the Rights Agreement to protect stockholder value by attempting to diminish the risk that our ability to use our NOLs to reduce potential future federal income tax obligations may become substantially limited.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Each Right entitles the registered holder to purchase from the Company one one-hundredth of a share of Series A Junior Participating Preferred Stock, par value $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_000759" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapSeriesAPreferredStockMember_20160518" decimals="INF">0.01</ix:nonFraction> per share (&#8220;Preferred Shares&#8221;), of the Company at a price of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_000760" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" contextRef="C_0001093082_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapSeriesAPreferredStockMember_20160518" decimals="INF">13.39</ix:nonFraction> per one one-hundredth of a Preferred Share, subject to adjustment.&#160;&#160;As a result of the Rights Agreement, any person or group that acquires beneficial ownership of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000761" name="hbp:CommonStockAcquisitionBeneficialOwnershipPercentage" contextRef="C_0001093082_20160517_20160518" decimals="4" scale="-2">4.99</ix:nonFraction>% or more of the Company&#8217;s common stock without the approval of the Board would be subject to significant dilution in the ownership interest of that person or group.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with entry into the Rights Agreement, on May 18, 2016, the Company filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware an Amended and Restated Certificate of Designation of Series A Junior Participating Preferred Stock to create the Preferred Shares.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:7.69%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000284" name="us-gaap:UnusualOrInfrequentItemsDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001093082_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000284_dcnt_3db110c9-63a2-498d-8093-1fbca9206730">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">18. IMPACT OF AND COMPANY RESPONSE TO COVID-19</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In March 2020, the World Health Organization recognized the novel strain of coronavirus, COVID-19, as a pandemic. The United States, various other countries and state and local jurisdictions have imposed, among other things, travel and business operation restrictions intended to limit the spread of the COVID-19 virus and have advised or required individuals to adhere to social distancing or limit or eliminate time spent outside of their homes. This pandemic and the governmental response have resulted in significant and widespread economic disruptions to, and uncertainty in, the global and U.S. economies, including in the regions in which the Company operates.&#160;&#160;In many jurisdictions, the Company and its customers were deemed &#8220;essential businesses&#8221; and continued to operate, reducing the impact of these restrictions on its operations and results for year ended December 31, 2020. However, the Company&#8217;s management cannot reliably predict the future impact of the pandemic and the governmental response to the pandemic on the Company&#8217;s operations and future results. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">With the exception of closing <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_hbpBranch" id="F_000784" name="hbp:NumberOfBranchesClosed" contextRef="C_0001093082_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> branches as a part of the Company&#8217;s restructuring efforts (as discussed in Note 17, &#8220;Restructuring&#8221;), all of the Company&#8217;s branches remain open and capable of meeting customer needs. The Company has taken protective measures to guard the health and well-being of its employees and customers, including the implementation of social distancing requirements and remote work options where possible. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has observed certain of its customers adjusting purchases and operations according to the impact of COVID-19 and governmental restrictions and has adjusted its own operations accordingly. The pandemic has had an adverse impact to the supply chain, with some of the Company&#8217;s vendors putting the Company on allocation as a result of reduced inventory and labor shortages resulting in longer lead-times for the fulfillment of certain products. Early in the pandemic, the Company adjusted its sales forecast and took proactive measures to protect its operating liquidity, including communicating with vendors and customers, seeking modification of payment and other terms of rental and procurement agreements and monitoring its accounts receivable. The Company initially reduced inventory levels to meet an anticipated decrease in demand and has continued to manage inventories according to regularly updated sales forecasts. The Company also implemented cost containment measures, including closing two of its branches, lay-offs, wage reductions, suspension of matching contributions to its qualified defined contribution plan, and eliminated non-essential spend. Wages were reinstated for substantially all employees in October 2020. The senior management team continued to have reduced compensation until early 2021. Additionally, the compensation paid to our Board of Directors continued at a reduced level until early 2021. The Company delayed or cancelled certain non-essential capital expenditures during 2020. The Company has utilized its diverse overseas network to source alternative suppliers of its proprietary products, while simultaneously rationalizing its purchase volume to better align with its current sales projections and to manage the supply chain. While the Company believes these actions mitigated the impact of the pandemic on its operations in 2020, it cannot provide any assurance that these actions will be successful if the pandemic continues to have a longer-term impact on the economy. As of December 31, 2020, the Company does not have any material outstanding deferred obligations to suppliers as deferred amounts have been substantially repaid.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">-49-</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" /><ix:continuation id="F_000284_dcnt_3db110c9-63a2-498d-8093-1fbca9206730">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="ITEM_9ACONTROLS_PROCEDURES">ITEM&#160;9A&#8212;CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures<span style="font-weight:normal;">&#8212;The Company, under the supervision and with the participation of our Disclosure Committee and management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, has evaluated the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rule 13a-15(e) under the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)).  Based upon that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures are effective as of December&#160;31, 2020 in all material respects in (a)&#160;causing information required to be disclosed by us in reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act to be recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms and (b)&#160;causing such information to be accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting<span style="font-weight:normal;">&#8212;The Company&#8217;s management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as such term is defined in Exchange Act Rules&#160;13a-15(f).  Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting based on the framework in </span><span style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework (2013)</span><span style="font-weight:normal;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. Management&#8217;s assessment included an evaluation of the design of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting and testing of the operational effectiveness of its internal control over financial reporting.  Management reviewed the results of its assessment with the Audit Committee of our Board of Directors.  Based on our evaluation under the framework in </span><span style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework (2013)</span><span style="font-weight:normal;">, our management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December&#160;31, 2020.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Because of inherent limitations, any system of internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect all misstatements.&#160;&#160;Projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of confidence with the policies and procedures may deteriorate.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no changes in the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting during the Company&#8217;s fiscal fourth quarter ended December&#160;31, 2020 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</p>
